stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy offers a nursing home's administrator free catering for staff events. Nothing is said about individual patients, but the pharmacy hopes the facility will send it more business. How does the regulation treat the arrangement?

choices.text: Permitted, because no referral of any individual patient is being solicited.
Permitted, because catering is not a payment of money.
Permitted if the facility discloses the arrangement to its residents.
Permitted if the value stays below the pharmacy's ordinary annual marketing budget.
Prohibited, because a licensee may not offer anything of value for the generation of business.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.01(11) bars a licensee from offering, soliciting or receiving remuneration or anything of value to or from any person who owns, operates, manages or is an employee of a hospital, nursing home or other health care facility in return for a referral or for the generation of business from the sale or furnishing of drugs, devices or services to such persons or institutions.

choice_analysis.A: Generation of business is covered separately from an individual referral.
choice_analysis.B: Anything of value is covered, not only money.
choice_analysis.C: Disclosure is not a stated cure.
choice_analysis.D: No de minimis or budget-based exception is provided.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: offering anything of value for the generation of business is prohibited.

related_facts: The prohibition runs in both directions, covering offering as well as receiving.
explanation.mpje_trap: The rule does not require a named patient or a cash payment; generation of business and anything of value suffice.

reasoning_steps: Identify the recipient as a manager of a health care facility
Classify the catering as anything of value
Apply the generation-of-business limb rather than looking for a named patient
